videos.script: Lesson 16 ran routing protocols inside one network, where every router is on the same side. {{recap}} The internet is tens of thousands of networks, run by different people, with different interests. They still have to tell each other what they can reach. That is BGP. {{bgp}} The lab is a company with its own address block and its own autonomous system number, connected to two providers. {{lab}} You will open a BGP session to each provider, and find that the router refuses to exchange anything until you write down what may go in and out. {{session}} Then you will read the AS path, the list of networks a route has crossed, and see why it decides which way traffic goes. {{path}} You will make the path longer on purpose, and watch one provider change its mind about how to reach you. {{prepend}} Then you will make a mistake on purpose: announce the wrong routes, and see the filter on the other side catch it. {{leak}} Last, the defences the real internet uses, from route filters to signed records of who owns which addresses. {{rpki}}
